literal: Desiring grace, he who stood in the path, if he desires wealth and schemes evil, will perish.
translation: He who stands in the path of virtue, desiring grace, will be ruined if he covets another's wealth and schemes evil deeds.
modern: அருளை விரும்பி அறவழியில் நிற்பவன், பிறர் பொருளை விரும்பித் தீயவற்றை எண்ணினால் கெட்டுப்போவான்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive nature of covetousness. A person who has committed themselves to a life of virtue and grace (அருள்) must maintain consistency in their thoughts. If such a person, driven by greed, covets another's property (பொருள்) and begins to plot evil schemes (பொல்லாத சூழ) to acquire it, they will lose their moral standing and be completely ruined (கெடும்). The contrast between desiring grace (அருள்வெஃகி) and desiring material wealth (பொருள்வெஃகி) shows that spiritual progress is instantly destroyed by the rise of greed.
